notes.title: Foreign buying
notes.text: Foreign investors bought nearly $3 billion of Indian shares in the week, including $1.6 billion on Thursday, their largest one-day purchase in nearly six years, Reuters reported, as funds moved out of technology-heavy markets. Provisional exchange data put foreign net buying at ₹32,210 crore from 2 to 5 Nov and domestic institutions' net selling at ₹18,228 crore.

notes.title: Oil
notes.text: Brent was on course for a weekly fall of about 12%, Reuters reported, after US midterm results raised hopes of de-escalation in the Iran conflict; tanker attacks in the Gulf lifted prices from two-month lows on Thursday and Friday. India imports most of its crude, so lower prices ease the import bill.

notes.title: Rupee and bonds
notes.text: The rupee rose 1.1% in the week to 93.905 per dollar, its strongest since 22 April and its best week in three, Reuters reported. The 10-year G-Sec yield closed at 7.17% on 5 Nov, 24 basis points lower in November, according to Business Standard.

notes.title: US election and rates
notes.text: Democrats won both houses of Congress; the Nasdaq then fell 5.52% on Thursday as chip and AI shares were sold. CME FedWatch pricing put the chance of a December US rate rise at 68% on Friday, Reuters reported.

brief: The NIFTY 50 rose 2.01% to 25,030.35 and the Sensex 2.17% to 81,028.02 on Friday, a seventh straight gain, as banks and financial shares led; mid and small caps slipped (Angel One, DSIJ).
For the week the NIFTY 50 rose 8.58% and the Sensex 8.82%, as foreign investors were net buyers in each session from 2 to 5 Nov (provisional) and the rupee firmed 1.1% (Reuters).
Asia fell sharply after Thursday's US technology sell-off: the Nikkei lost 5.96% and the Kospi 6.02%.
Next week: Muhurat trading on Sunday 8 Nov, NSE closed on Tuesday 10 Nov, US inflation on 10 Nov and India's on 12 Nov.

drivers.title: Results season
drivers.text: Hindalco and Bosch reported September-quarter profit growth on Friday, and Mahindra & Mahindra led the NIFTY 50 after its results. Company earnings feed into index-level earnings, one of the measures used to assess equity valuations.

drivers.title: Inflation backdrop
drivers.text: Consumer price inflation was 5.54% in September (provisional), up from 4.83% in August, according to MoSPI data. Inflation shapes the RBI's rate decisions, which reach bond yields and borrowing costs.

global_cues.title: Technology sell-off
global_cues.text: The selling in US chip and AI shares spread to Asia on Friday. Large global moves reach India through foreign portfolio flows and the pricing of Indian IT shares; Reuters linked this week's foreign buying of Indian shares to India's small exposure to AI chips.

events.title: US jobs report
events.text: The consensus forecast cited by Kiplinger puts October payroll growth at about 59,000, after 29,000 in September, with unemployment at 4.2%. US data moves Treasury yields and the dollar.

global.headline: US chip and AI shares fell for a second day on Thursday, and Tokyo and Seoul lost about 6% on Friday
global.note: A drop of more than 8% in the Kospi set off a 20-minute trading halt (Aju Press). Europe's STOXX 600 was down 1.6% in early trade on Friday (Reuters); European and US closes for Friday come after this edition.

us.title: The session
us.text: AI and chip shares fell for a second day on Thursday; the Philadelphia semiconductor index lost more than 12% and Nvidia about 9.3%, Fox Business reported. An eToro analyst quoted by Fox Business, Jakub Rochlitz, pointed to calls from some Democrats to restrict new data-centre projects.

events.title: US rate expectations
events.text: CME FedWatch pricing put the chance of a December Fed rate rise at 68% on Friday, Reuters reported, and Goldman Sachs cut its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150 an ounce from $4,650, citing a firmer Fed. US rates reach India through the dollar and foreign flows.

events.title: Gulf shipping
events.text: Iran said three more tankers were attacked on Thursday, Reuters reported, which lifted Brent from two-month lows. Crude reaches India through the import bill and the rupee.

metals.headline: IBJA's Friday rates for gold and silver were below Thursday's closing rates; spot gold fell about 1% as oil rose

international.label: Spot gold
international.detail: Still on course for its best week since late August (Reuters)

commentary.text: Gold fell on Friday as rebounding crude revived inflation concerns, Tastylive's Ilya Spivak told Reuters; KCM Trade's Tim Waterer said some investors sold gold to cover margin calls during the technology sell-off.

Central banks bought an estimated 321 tonnes of gold in the July to September quarter, led by China and Poland, and global gold ETF holdings fell for a fourth straight day, Mirae Asset Sharekhan's Praveen Singh said in Business Standard.

highlights.text: Among equity categories, small cap funds took in a net ₹9,038.57 crore in September, mid cap funds ₹7,834.84 crore and flexi cap funds ₹6,701.80 crore. Large cap funds drew ₹859.47 crore, while ELSS funds saw a net outflow of ₹662.14 crore.
Passive funds took in a net ₹11,887 crore, including equity ETFs ₹9,960 crore, gold ETFs ₹4,451 crore and silver ETFs ₹1,974 crore.

nfo_summary.text: Five new fund offers remain open into next week, according to Cafemutual: a silver ETF and a silver fund of funds, a realty index fund, an energy ETF and a fixed maturity plan. Each scheme's category, riskometer level and terms are in its scheme information document. This list is reported for information only and is not a recommendation.

regulatory.text: Since 1 November, direct plans are the default option on fund houses' own digital platforms, and investors who choose a regular plan there are told it carries a higher expense ratio. Regular plans remain available.

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's categorisation rules, a small cap fund is an open-ended equity scheme that must keep at least 65% of its total assets in the shares of small cap companies, which SEBI defines as the 251st listed company onwards by full market capitalisation. SEBI's circular of 26 February 2026 kept the 65% minimum. These are equity schemes, so their value rises and falls with the share prices of smaller companies, and each scheme's riskometer level is set out in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: What a weekly change measures
paragraphs: A weekly change compares one Friday's closing level with the previous Friday's close, so it shows where the week ended, not how far prices moved along the way.
This week the NIFTY 50 went from 23,053.10 on 30 Oct to 25,030.35 on 6 Nov, a change of 8.58%, though no single day rose that much.
A fund's factsheet reports returns over set periods in the same way, from one date to another; past performance may or may not be sustained in future.
